verdict.rationale: Linear's first-party changelog documents Loops as recurring agent workflows. Users describe a job in plain language and choose whether it runs on a schedule or in response to an event, so this is a genuine recurring schedule, not a one-off action. Loops also respond to workspace activity and can update docs or post to Slack. Missing for 10: details of schedule configuration (frequency/cron granularity, time zones, run history or failure handling), programmatic/API management of scheduled loops, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can schedule recurring jobs or workflows

citations.quote: Loops are a new way for Linear Agent to take on recurring work for your team. Describe the job in plain language and then choose whether it should run on a schedule or in response to an event.
Loops are recurring agent workflows for teams. They now respond to more workspace activity, including changes to initiatives, projects, and cycles.
use Loops to keep docs and project descriptions up-to-date
